heroHeadline: Khartoum Airport Reopens After 4-Day RSF Drone Closure; SAF Drone Kills 5 at Market in North Kordofan
heroSubtitle: On Day 1120, Sudan's Civil Aviation Authority reopened Khartoum International Airport with Badr Airlines resuming flights — ending the four-day closure forced by RSF/UAE drone attacks on May 4–5 that Sudan has formally attributed to UAE-supplied munitions launched from Bahir Dar Airport, Ethiopia. Tarco Aviation and Sudanair are set to resume capital routes on May 10. Sudan's UNSC evidence campaign linking the attacks to the UAE and Ethiopia continues, with both nations maintaining denial. Separately, a SAF drone struck a market in Abu Zaima, North Kordofan, killing at least 5 civilians — the latest strike in the near-daily aerial campaign by both sides that has killed over 700 civilians in North and South Kordofan alone in Q1 2026. Sudan's Ethiopian border remains on high alert with SAF troops and anti-aircraft systems deployed to East Gallabat, Basunda, and Al-Fashaga. The UN and UK condemnations of the Khartoum airport RSF drone attacks from May 8 stand as the most recent formal international statements on the escalation. Sudan's civil war continues into its fourth year with 14 million displaced, an estimated 150,000+ killed, and 34 million in urgent humanitarian need.
